terms.def: A named location used to hold a value that can change.
A reusable block of code that performs a specific task.
terms.hint: A named tool you can call again.

terms.def: A control structure that repeats instructions while a condition holds or for a set number of times.
A collection where the most recently added item is removed first (LIFO).
A collection where the earliest added item is removed first (FIFO).
An indexed collection of elements, usually of the same type.
A finite sequence of well-defined steps for solving a problem.
A data type with the logical values true and false.
An organised collection of data that can be stored, queried, and updated.
A field or set of fields that uniquely identifies each row in a database table.
terms.hint: A unique student ID in a student table.

terms.def: A data type representing a sequence of characters.
A data type representing whole numbers without a fractional part.

links.why: The last plate placed is the first removed. A stack operates in last-in, first-out order.
The first person to join is served first. A queue uses first-in, first-out order.
The label names the value. Unlike a physical container, its type rules depend on the programming language.
Instructions repeat. A programming loop has a condition or count; an analogy alone does not specify termination.
A function performs a defined task when called; unlike an appliance it is a block of code.
An index selects an element, like a locker number; array elements obey programming-language type rules.
Both specify ordered steps; an algorithm must be precise enough to execute and terminate.
True and false are two logical values; a Boolean does not represent brightness levels.
Records can be stored and queried; a database also enforces structure and supports updates.
The key distinguishes one row from every other row; names alone need not be unique.
Characters have an order, like beads; strings represent text rather than physical objects.
Integers represent whole numbers, including negatives and zero; they do not represent fractions.

detectives.q: A text editor must undo the most recent action first. Which data structure fits?
detectives.why: A stack removes the last action added first (LIFO), matching undo order.

detectives.q: A printer should process jobs in the order they arrive. Which structure fits?
detectives.why: A queue serves the earliest job first (FIFO).

detectives.q: You repeat the same tax calculation in five places. How can you organise it?
detectives.why: A function packages a specific task so you can call it repeatedly instead of duplicating code.

detectives.q: A program must check every item in a shopping list. What structure repeats the check?
detectives.why: A loop repeats instructions for each item, or until a condition changes.

detectives.q: Every student row needs a unique identifier. Which database feature serves this purpose?
detectives.why: A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot contain null values.

detectives.q: A game needs to store a player's changing score. What named storage should it use?
detectives.why: A variable holds a value that may change.

detectives.q: You access the fifth item using its index. Which collection is being used?
detectives.why: An array provides indexed access to its elements.

detectives.q: A program stores whether a user is signed in as true or false. Which type fits?
detectives.why: A Boolean represents one of two logical values.

detectives.q: A library needs to store and query thousands of book records. What should organise them?
detectives.why: A database stores organised data and supports queries.

detectives.q: You specify a finite, precise set of steps to sort numbers. What have you described?
detectives.why: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined steps.

detectives.q: A form stores the text of a person's name. Which data type fits?
detectives.why: A string represents a sequence of characters.

detectives.q: A counter tracks a whole number of available seats. Which type fits?
detectives.why: An integer represents whole numbers without fractional parts.

story: A Variable holds a ticket number as an Integer, while a String holds the visitor's name. A Function follows an Algorithm to process the ticket. A Loop visits each entry in an Array. A Boolean records whether entry is allowed. A Queue serves visitors in arrival order, while a Stack holds actions that can be undone. A Database stores each visitor under a unique Primary key.

robots.q: Explain the difference between a Stack and a Queue.
robots.example: A stack removes the most recently added item first (LIFO). A queue removes the earliest added item first (FIFO).

robots.q: What does a Function do, and why would you use one?
robots.example: A function is a named block of code that performs a specific task. You can call it repeatedly, which allows reuse and reduces duplicate code.

rules.name: A block of code or instructions

robots.q: Explain a Loop and how it stops.
robots.example: A loop repeats instructions. A condition or count controls repetition. It stops when the condition is false or the count is reached.

rules.name: Controlled by a condition or count

robots.example: A variable is named storage for a value that can change.

robots.q: Explain how an array organises its elements.
robots.example: An array is an ordered collection whose elements can be accessed by index.

robots.q: What makes a procedure an algorithm?
robots.example: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined steps for solving a problem.

robots.q: Explain a Boolean and give its two values.
robots.example: A Boolean is a logical data type whose values are true and false.

robots.q: What is a database used for?
robots.example: A database stores organised data that can be queried and updated.

robots.q: Explain why a table needs a primary key.
robots.example: A primary key uniquely identifies each row of a database table.
A string is an ordered sequence of characters used to represent text.

robots.q: How does an integer differ from a fractional number?
robots.example: An integer represents a whole number without a fractional part.

robots.q: Why is choosing a queue useful for first-come-first-served requests?
robots.example: A queue uses FIFO so the earliest request is handled first.
